note: One row per Coach Brief or Coaching Module. A row is all a new brief or module needs: build_goalie_cards.py copies it into goalie-cards-data.js, and its card exists. Takeaways and grades are written by the Research Agent and state only what the page's studies found; the three questions match the page's Try it this week section.

items.title: Glove Positioning Analysis
items.takeaway: In a lab study of 14 recreational goalies, glove errors were largest on wide pucks near the face-off dots, and the glove drifted back toward the goal line from about the third rep.
questions: On which rep did the glove first drift back?
Did your goalie notice it? Ask them before you show the video.
What will you change in the sequence next week?

items.title: What the constraints-led approach is, and isn't
items.takeaway: A 2025 review of 9 mostly soccer studies found constraints-led practice did not cost technique and may build better game decisions. No hockey goalie has been in a trial, and lasting learning was barely tested.
questions: What did the goalie change without being told?
What did they say they were looking at?
What will you change in the drill next time?

items.title: Constraints: individual, task, environment
items.takeaway: A 2020 meta-analysis found that changing a constraint (individual, task or environment) reliably changes what athletes do. Whether that turns into lasting learning, and which change suits which goalie problem, is untested.
questions: Which constraint did you change, and which kind was it?
What did the goalie do differently in the first five reps? In the last five?
Did you give fewer cues than usual?

items.title: Representative practice: reps that look like games
items.takeaway: Expert hockey goalies place their last look before a save on the puck or stick (70.5% of trials, against 2.1% on the shooter's body), and late looks conceded more deflection goals. No study has tested whether more game-like goalie practice improves learning.
questions: What did the goalie look at before and after the change?
Did their success rate drop at first?
Was the drill still useful at a lower score on game day?

items.title: Designing a session with PoST
items.takeaway: PoST is an expert planning framework from soccer goalkeeping that labels each block of practice by stage and by how game-like and how hard it is. No study in any sport has tested it, and nobody has applied it to hockey.
questions: Label: which stage was each block of last week's practice?
Redesign: which block did you move, and how?
Film: what did the video show?

items.title: Is it working? Learning vs performance
items.takeaway: Practice performance can mislead in both directions, so learning shows up when a skill is checked cold a week later, not at the end of the drill. Save % needs about 3,000 shots to be half signal, so process measures such as freeze rate are steadier for tracking a habit.
